Ivanivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ivanivka, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery's founding is undocumented, though it appears on a 1917 Russian map, suggesting early 20th-century operation; it was likely demolished after WWII and subsequently built over. Ivanivka's Jewish population reached 1,438 (75% of residents) by 1897; a Jewish elementary school operated during the Soviet era, though the community fell to 353 (19%) by 1939. German-Romanian forces occupied the town in August 1941, murdering 342 Jews shortly after (29 local residents and 319 Moldavian refugees); four Jewish children were killed in August 1943. In total, 526 Jews were executed during the occupation.
